name: Telemetry
description: Readings over time as a Core platform domain (docs/phases/42-telemetry): one row per message per retention class on db:time_series (TimescaleDB where present), the per-tenant key dictionary, the latest value per entity and key, 1-minute aggregates with hour and day rollups, retention per tenant and kind, the TelemetryWriter every kind writes through, the read service and API (latest, series by range: raw, minute, hour, day), a dashboard data source, a generic save node, the tenant purge and the plan-driven class switch. A module contributes an entity kind (telemetry:entity_kind) to store its readings; the IoT package registers iot_device on top of this store.

permissions.name: Read telemetry readings (each kind decides which entities)
View the telemetry store (kinds, retention bindings, keys)

author: Kuray Karaaslan

extensionPoints.description: A module declares an entity kind whose readings the store keeps (telemetry.kinds.ts `TelemetryEntityKind`): the kind name (`iot_device`, `fx.currency`), its keys (declared, or open with its own key rule and cap), its retention (a fixed class, or a resolver for plan-driven classes), `canRead(ctx, entityIds)` (record-level read check, default deny), whether dashboards may list it, whether a flow or a binding may write it (`acceptsExternalWrites`, narrowed by `canWrite`), its lane (table family) and its per-tenant write budget. Default export is the kind. The writer refuses an unregistered kind; every read path asks the kind's canRead. The registry of kinds is loaded on first use through the generated loaders (lazyContributors), so any module may contribute a kind without a contribution-chain cycle (analytics does, while automation contributes to analytics and telemetry to automation).

metadata.label: Telemetry: raw message tables and 1-minute aggregates per retention class, hour and day rollups

extensions.description: Full-load lane only: two keys, raw messages, minute rows, latest values and job state for a synthetic entity of the inert kind telemetry.seed, so every telemetry table is filled in the guarded test database even without a module that owns a kind. The default seed leaves readings to their producers (exempt as runtime-state).

telemetry.latest (an entity's latest values as a record) and telemetry.series (keys over the board window, aggregated per bucket); only kinds that expose themselves, every execution through the kind's canRead for the viewer (cached per user).
action.save_reading on the generic host: a flow stores msg.payload as a reading of an entity of a kind that accepts flow writes; one writer call per wave.
Deletes the tenant's rows from every lane's tables (raw, minute, hour and day rollups, latest, state, hints), its class bindings and its key dictionary, then its Redis key hash.

Phase 57 wave 1: readings on the telemetry MCP server (/api/mcp/telemetry), read only: get_latest_readings and get_reading_series (at most 31 days, 10 keys, 500 points a key). Permission telemetry.read and the kind's own canRead, as on the read routes; device values reach the model fenced as untrusted. Imports only the contract from common.
